evidence.observation: Bootstrap pass. Before loading anything it calls this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) and reloads settings, then resolves the extension set via loadCurrentExtensionSet. Project-scoped resources (including <cwd>/.pi/extensions) are therefore withheld while user/global and temporary CLI extensions still load, which is exactly why the fresh project fixture is absent during bootstrap.

Only when the caller supplies options.resolveProjectTrust does reload run the pre-trust bootstrap pass (line 452), ask the caller for a boolean (line 453), and adopt it with this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted) (line 454) before reloading settings and re-resolving packages. That explicit callback return value is the sole switch that lets project-scoped extensions become available; without it the bootstrap pass is skipped entirely.

Builds the bootstrap extension set from this.packageManager.resolve() under the current trust state and feeds the resulting paths to loadExtensionsCached. Because resolution happens after the trust flag is forced off, the project fixture path is never part of the bootstrap set; the same path only appears once reload has applied a trusted decision.

The same trust signal gates another project-scoped resource: the project .pi/SYSTEM.md is only returned when this.settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() is true, otherwise only the global agent-dir file is considered. This confirms project resources share one explicit trust decision rather than per-resource opt-ins.

claims.claim: During the bootstrap pass, DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions forces the project untrusted (setProjectTrusted(false)) before resolving extensions, so a fresh project extension under <cwd>/.pi/extensions is not loaded while user/global extensions remain available, and the untrusted project extension module body never executes.

A project extension becomes available only after DefaultResourceLoader.reload receives an explicit trusted boolean from the resolveProjectTrust callback and applies it via setProjectTrusted, after which packageManager.resolve() exposes the project-scoped extension path.

loadCurrentExtensionSet is the single place the bootstrap extension set is built and it re-resolves resources under the current trust state, so the same fixture path is absent from the pre-trust result and present in the post-trust result.
Other project-scoped resources share the same signal: discoverSystemPromptFile only reads the project .pi/SYSTEM.md when settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() is true.

conclusion: The demo fixture packages/coding-agent/test/fixtures/trust-bootstrap/project/.pi/extensions/fresh-extension.ts is a project-scoped extension. The executable demo packages/coding-agent/test/trust-bootstrap-demo.test.ts drives the real DefaultResourceLoader and shows the required contract: (1) during the bootstrap pass (loadProjectTrustExtensions) only the user/global extension loads and the project extension's module body never runs (load counter 0); (2) at the moment the explicit resolveProjectTrust callback is invoked the project extension is still absent; (3) only after the callback returns true does reload apply setProjectTrusted(true) and the project extension load exactly once; (4) a rejected decision (false) keeps it unavailable. The gating is implemented by resource-loader.ts forcing/receiving the project trust flag before package resolution, so no project-scoped extension can load without the explicit trusted decision.
